newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch ING buys Equitable of Iowa for $2.2 billion.
newsitem.headline: Dutch ING buys Equitable of Iowa for $2.2 billion.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV said Tuesday it was expanding its U.S. insurance holdings, adding Equitable of Iowa Cos. in a $2.2 billion deal.

Although the bid, worth $68 a share, is the Dutch firm's largest takeover to date, the banking and insurance group said its appetite for expansion remained and it reaffirmed plans to expand further in the United States and Europe.
Executive Chairman Aad Jacobs said ING's ambition to be one of the top 10 life insurance companies in the United States had not been satisfied by the acquisition, taking it only into the top 20.
Jacobs also said ING was working hard to expand in corporate banking in Europe, particularly in Germany and France, and it still intended to buy a U.S. investment bank.
The takeover of Equitable of Iowa, which is based in Des Moines, was long anticipated by the market in view of the group's growing cash mountain, estimated at up to $5 billion.
"In terms of product mix, distribution channels and geographic spread, Equitable of Iowa complements ING's existing life insurance business in an excellent way," ING said.
Equitable provides life insurance and individual annuity products, mainly to middle-class consumers and small businesses, throughout the United States.

The deal, set to take effect in the fourth quarter pending shareholder and regulatory approval, is ING's biggest acquisition since the group was formed through a merger of NMB Postbank with insurer Nationale Nederlanden in 1991.
ING said it planned to pay for up to 60 percent of the purchase in ING stock. The rest would be paid in borrowed funds.
"We are a very rich company and we can afford to make a number of steps forward," Jacobs said in a telephone interview.
He said the acquisition would boost ING's earnings by about 1 percent in the first year and roughly double ING's U.S. life insurance premium income to $4.3 billion.

ING spokesman Ruud Polet said that ING's North American life insurance operations were active in the higher and lower income segments of the market while the Iowa company was strong in the middle segment. "It's a perfect fit in terms of segment," he said.
The company owns Life of Georgia and Southland Life, both based in Atlanta, Security Life of Denver and other insurance and investment companies in the United States and Canada.

ING, which had long indicated its interest in making another U.S. life insurance acquisition, had been looking specifically at Equitable of Iowa for a couple of months, he said. The acquisition has the backing of the Equitable of Iowa board.
Investors cheered the news, sending ING shares soaring on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange. They rose 6 guilders to trade at 102.10 in the afternoon.

Analysts were also upbeat on the deal, although some said it was expensive. Equitable of Iowa's stock closed Monday at $57.375, meaning ING was offering an 18.5 percent premium to Equitable shareholders.
"It's a good strategic move, notably because it will increase the stability of ING's earnings, since the proportion of life insurance gets bigger," said Bart van der Feen, banking analyst with IRIS.
"The deal looks positive," agreed Delta Lloyd Bank's Dennis Ederzeel. "But you can argue that the price is high. ING is paying 17 times next year's profit for Iowa."
But he added that ING could afford paying a premium in view of its own high price/earnings ratio of close to 21 times earnings.
